{"front":"Management","back":"Defined as the creative problem solving process of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling an organization's resources to achieve its mission and objectives."}
{"front":"Engineering Management","back":"Refers to the activity combining technical knowledge with the ability to organize and coordinate worker power, materials, machinery, and money."}
{"front":"Decision-Making","back":"The process of identifying and choosing alternative courses of action in a manner appropriate to the demands of the situation."}
{"front":"Planning","back":"The management function that involves anticipating future trends and determining the best strategies and tactics to achieve organizational objectives."}
{"front":"Strategic Plan","back":"Covers the major goals of the entire organization."}
{"front":"Intermediate/Tactical Plan","back":"Concerned in developing very detailed strategies about what needs to be done, who should do it, and how it should be done."}
{"front":"Operational Plan","back":"The plan that a manager uses to accomplish his or her job responsibilities; developed to support tactical plans."}
{"front":"Contingency Plan (Plan B)","back":"Involves alternative courses of action when the original plans that have been developed do not achieve the goals of the organization."}
{"front":"Organizing","back":"A management function which refers to the structuring of resources and activities to accomplish objectives in an efficient and effective manner."}
{"front":"Organizational Chart","back":"A diagram that shows the structure of an organization and the relationships and relative ranks of its positions."}
{"front":"Staffing","back":"The management function that determines human resource needs, recruits, selects, trains, and develops human resources for jobs created by an organization."}
{"front":"Recruitment","back":"The attempt to attract candidates to apply for the vacant positions in the company."}
{"front":"Selection","back":"The step where individuals most likely to succeed on the job are chosen; may include interviews, reference checks, and physical examination."}
{"front":"Induction and Orientation","back":"The process that includes introduction of the new employee to the work group and acquainting him with the organization's policies and rules."}
{"front":"Training and Development","back":"Concerned with improvement of the employee's skills (training) and preparation for additional responsibility (development)."}
{"front":"Performance Appraisal","back":"A system that measures the actual performance of the employee compared to designated standards."}
{"front":"Directing","back":"Influencing people's behaviour through motivation, communication, group dynamics, leadership and discipline."}

{"front":"Controlling","back":"Refers to the process of ascertaining whether organizational objectives have been achieved and determining what activities should then be taken to achieve objectives better in the future."}
{"front":"Communication","back":"A process of sharing information through symbols, including words and message."}
{"front":"Motivating","back":"Refers to the process of activating behaviour, sustaining it, and directing it toward a particular goal."}
{"front":"Leading","back":"Exhibiting skills to get others to play an effective part in achieving plans."}
{"front":"Autocratic Leadership","back":"Style where all the decision-making powers are centralized in one person and the leader can make decisions without consulting others."}
{"front":"Democratic Leadership","back":"Style where subordinates are included in the decision-making and the leader gives instructions after consulting the group."}
{"front":"Free-Rein Leadership","back":"Style where most decisions are left to the subordinates and the leader leaves the group entirely to itself."}
{"front":"Operation","back":"Refers to any process that accepts inputs and uses resources to change those inputs in useful ways."}
{"front":"Operations Management","back":"The process of planning, organizing, and controlling operations to reach objectives efficiently and effectively."}
{"front":"Marketing","back":"A group of activities designed to facilitate and expedite the selling of goods and services."}
{"front":"Product","back":"Any goods and services that satisfy the needs and wants of consumers; anything tangible or intangible that can be offered for purchase."}
{"front":"Price","back":"The amount of money that consumers are willing to pay for a product or service."}
{"front":"Promotion","back":"A communication process that takes place between a business and end-users, consumers and external parties."}
{"front":"Place","back":"Refers to having the right product, in the right location, at the right time to be purchased by consumers."}
{"front":"People (Marketing Mix)","back":"All people who directly or indirectly influence the perceived value of the product or service, including knowledge workers, employees, and management."}
{"front":"Process (Marketing Mix)","back":"The way in which orders are handled, customers are satisfied and the service is delivered."}
{"front":"Physical Evidence","back":"Tangible evidence of the service customers will receive."}
{"front":"Finance","back":"Responsible for the procurement and administration of funds with the view of achieving the objectives of the business."}
{"front":"Risk","back":"Refers to the uncertainty concerning loss or injury."}
{"front":"Risk Management","back":"An organized strategy for protecting and conserving assets and people."}
